transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-26
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Lopez (VectorHealth CTO), Jordan Kim (VectorHealth ML Eng), Priya Rao (VectorHealth Security), Ethan Park (VectorHealth Product)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on model selection and version pinning after last week's benchmark. Reviewed latency/cost tradeoffs for 7B vs 13B variants, discussed pinning strategy, rollback/fallback policies, and next steps for security sign-off and canary.

Topics: model selection, quantization profile effects, pinning mechanics, fallback chain, security/KMS, canary rollout plan, benchmarking next steps

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone — thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Lopez: Hey this is Maya, I'm here.
[00:07] Jordan Kim: Jordan here.
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya.
[00:09] Ethan Park: Ethan.
[00:10] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood. Lena's on as well.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: yep hey all.
[00:15] Avery Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: review the benchmark snapshot Samir sent, discuss model pinning strategy, fallback/rollback, and security questions. Samir, do you want to walk the perf numbers?
[00:26] Samir Patel: Sure. So we ran the same 500 sample conversational suite you guys shared, plus the 1k synth set — results in the spreadsheet. Short version: 7B int8 quantized hits median latency 80 to 110ms per request in our hosted baseline, 13B int8 is around 130 to 190ms. When you move to dedicated GPUs with our batching profile tuned, 13B drops to 70 to 95ms median but cost per 1k tokens goes up about 2.3x compared to 7B on dedicated. There was a slight degradation in hallucination rate on some intent categories for the 7B, specifically in multi-step clinical note summarization.
[01:10] Jordan Kim: Hmm, the hallucinations on clinical notes are our main blocker. Any chance the 7B gap is from the quantization profile? We used q4_0 for the 7B runs.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Good call — the q4_0 profile helps density but can hurt rare-token fidelity. We did an additional run with q8_0-lite on the 7B and hallucinations dropped by, like, 14% relative. Latency bumped ~15ms. So tradeoff there.
[01:36] Priya Rao: From security — we noticed the logs in the spreadsheet show full request text in the hosted run. We need to confirm retention is off for POC and if KMS encrypts at rest.
[01:46] Avery Chen: Yes — for POC we can disable request retention; Samir can share the flag and we will send the SOC2 packet. The hosted offering has AES-256 at rest and KMS optional; Dedicated/Private gives you customer-managed keys and HSM options.
[02:02] Maya Lopez: On pinning — we're leaning to pin to the 13B on dedicated for our pilot because of latency once dedicated tuning is applied, but we worry about cost. Can we do hybrid: default to 7B, but pin critical clinical workflows to 13B?
[02:18] Samir Patel: Absolutely. Our routing supports per-route pinning. You can set a route to always go to a pinned model version on a dedicated pool; other routes fall back to hosted 7B for cost efficiency. Also we support a fallback chain: pinned -> model variant (e.g., 13B quantized variant) -> 7B hosted if capacity constrained.
[02:36] Jordan Kim: How does automatic rollback work if the pinned model starts regressing on quality after a rollout?
[02:41] Samir Patel: Two layers: first, you can enable automatic rollback based on eval signals — we run your golden prompt set at intervals and if quality drops by X% we trigger an alert and can auto-revert traffic to prior model. Second, we have a canary window: rollouts are gradual and you can set thresholds for latency and correctness.
[02:58] Ethan Park: Quick question — for the canary, what's the minimum traffic slice you do? We want to avoid impacting customers.
[03:05] Samir Patel: We support as small as 0.5% sampling for canaries. Typically customers start at 1-5%.
[03:10] Maya Lopez: Jordan, for your evals, can you run the PII-sensitive subset on both 13B dedicated and 7B hosted? We need to see precision/recall on entity redaction tasks.
[03:19] Jordan Kim: Yep that's on my list — will run and upload results.
[03:22] Priya Rao: Also on encryption — if we go dedicated with customer-managed keys, can we rotate keys without downtime?
[03:29] Samir Patel: Key rotation for CMKs is seamless; we support staged rotation and re-encryption hooks, there shouldn't be downtime. We'll include the KMS rotation steps in the security packet.
[03:38] Lena Ortiz: Quick note — we observed an odd spike in tail latency on the 13B dedicated run at 2x token lengths; Samir, you mentioned kernel selection might cause that?
[03:47] Samir Patel: Right — the runtime picks kernels based on sequence length distribution. For long sequences we sometimes see higher tail latency until the next kernel switch; we can pre-warm the pool with a few long requests or use sequence-aware routing to isolate long requests. That reduces the spike.
[04:05] Maya Lopez: Okay, sounds like a plan. On pinning config, will we get a sample YAML?
[04:09] Samir Patel: Yes, I'll send a sample pinning config plus fallback chain. It includes per-route model, primary pool, fallback models, and automatic rollback thresholds.
[04:18] Jordan Kim: One more thing — regarding token accounting and cost attribution, will the dedicated model count tokens separately from hosted? We need per-route billing mapping to our internal product metrics.
[04:27] Avery Chen: We can map token-level cost to route tags and export that to your data warehouse. Lena, can you add that to action items?
[04:34] Lena Ortiz: Added.
[04:36] Ethan Park: Are there any concerns about vendor lock if we pin to a specific 13B variant? We may want the ability to swap to a different 13B family quickly.
[04:45] Samir Patel: You can pin at the model version level or model family level. If you pin to family, you get more flexibility — roll forward to compatible variants. We recommend pinning to a verified version for production-critical routes, and family-level for non-critical ones.
[04:58] Maya Lopez: Let's walk through a hypothetical fault: dedicated pool hits memory error and becomes unavailable mid-shift. How does request routing behave?
[05:07] Samir Patel: Automatic fallback — requests are routed to the next available compatible model. If dedicated is down we route to hosted 13B or fallback 7B depending on your chain. There's also a warm standby option where we keep a minimal pool for critical routes.
[05:20] Priya Rao: For auditability we need detailed access logs with SAML SSO identity mapped. Is that supported?
[05:27] Samir Patel: Yes, RBAC and SSO mapping available for Dedicated and Private. We'll include sample logs in the security packet.
[05:34] Jordan Kim: On the hallucination metric — what's the measurement? Is it human-labeled or automated? Our current sheet shows a 'hallucination rate' column but not methodology.
[05:42] Samir Patel: For these POC runs we used a hybrid: automated heuristics for entity mismatch plus 150 human spot checks for high-risk intents. We'll document the exact rubric in the sheet.
[05:53] Maya Lopez: Good. For next week's deliverables — I want to see the 1k PII eval and the cost projections with route-level mapping. Also please show an example rollback event timeline.
[06:02] Avery Chen: We'll get that. Samir, Lena — anything else?
[06:06] Samir Patel: I'll add the pinning YAML and fallback examples and the kernel/sequence mitigation notes.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: I'll update the spreadsheet with the tail-latency notes and per-route cost mapping.
[06:18] Priya Rao: We'll prepare the kiosk list of KMS/HSM questions and get back with any blockers.
[06:24] Ethan Park: One smaller ask — can Redwood run a quick demo of the canary rollout UI? It helps stakeholders see the controls.
[06:30] Avery Chen: Yep we can schedule a short demo; I'll propose 30 minutes next week after you see the updated results.
[06:36] Maya Lopez: Ok thanks everyone. Quick recap?
[06:40] Avery Chen: Recap: Samir send pinning YAML + fallback by Jan 29; Avery to share perf & security packet by Jan 28; Jordan to run 1k PII eval by Feb 2; plan canary week of Feb 9 pending results.
[06:53] Jordan Kim: Sounds good.
[06:55] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[06:57] Samir Patel: Thanks all, talk soon.
[07:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and ASR artifacts; references to q4_0/q8_0-lite quantization profiles are approximate naming; the team agreed on hybrid pinning strategy and a canary-first rollout with auto-rollback thresholds.
